title: Synthetic Workset Orchestrator and Customer Onramp Checklist
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Goal: Build a repeatable, tenant-aware synthetic workload orchestrator ("Workset Orchestrator") and an evidence bundle/acceptance checklist that product and SEs can use to certify a customer's Dedicated capacity. The orchestrator must produce reproducible throughput signatures, per-tenant QoS vectors, and a concise acceptance artifact (CSV + dashboard links + deterministic run artifacts) that demonstrates the customer's committed throughput and tail latency guarantees. This ticket covers harness design, benchmarking methodology, automated evidence packaging, and the customer acceptance checklist.
scope: Design and implement a configurable load driver that can: 1) play back sanitized real-traffic traces; 2) synthesize tenant mixes (latency-sensitive vs throughput-heavy); 3) vary prompt length/token distributions; 4) simulate KV cache warm/cold scenarios; 5) produce deterministic seedable runs and reproducible metrics export. Produce automation to collect: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, batch size histogram, KV cache hit-rate, per-tenant error rates, and request-level sample traces for debugging.
success_criteria: Orchestrator can reproduce a target throughput signature within ±5% for 3 consecutive runs (same random seed)
Automated evidence package contains: run manifest, raw logs, aggregated metrics CSV, perf flamegraphs (if applicable), and dashboard snapshot link
Customer acceptance checklist lists deterministic pass/fail gates and can be executed by Solutions Engineers without code changes
Run duration, artifacts, and cost estimate are documented and fit into a single customer onboarding session (<= 4 hours)
Integration hooks for console trace links and alerting exist (trace IDs + run_id correlation)
benchmarking_methodology: 1) Calibration: Use a short (10–15m) calibration run to find the request rate that yields target 95th latency at desired load. 2) Signature capture: Run 3x 30m steady-state runs using same seed and traffic mix; capture percentile latencies, tokens/s, GPU util and memory. 3) Stress and degradation: Apply microbursts and sustained increases to detect autoscaler thresholds and QoS violations. 4) Warm/cold KV cache sweep: Run two passes—cold start and warmed—to measure cache delta. 5) Tenant isolation: Inject background tenants with configurable QPS to validate isolation and scheduler fairness. 6) Evidence: Save manifests, deterministic seed, and metric exports to artifact storage and attach dashboard snapshots.
testbed_config: Reference hardware profiles: rtx-gpu-small (single-GPU), rtx-gpu-large (multi-GPU), nvlink-64 (multi-GPU NVLink). Default test fleet config uses 4 nodes of rtx-gpu-large with batcher tuned to target 60–80% GPU utilization. Workload generator supports concurrent workers, per-worker rate limit, and per-tenant routing tags. Default model profiles: gptx-7b-quant, gptx-13b, and gptx-70b-quantized; sequence lengths are configurable between 64–2048 tokens. All runs include Prometheus + Cortex metrics and perf traces pushed to the run artifact bucket.
acceptance_checklist: Run manifest present and uploaded to artifacts storage
Three steady-state runs completed with run_id present in artifact bundle
p95 latency across runs <= customer SLA target (+5% tolerance for synthetic overhead)
No unhandled errors > 0.1% of requests during steady-state
Autoscaler never triggered an unsafe scale-down (documented in run logs)
KV cache hit-rate measured and annotated (if customer relies on prefix caching)
Per-tenant QoS violations documented and root cause annotated
SE signoff logged in comments with evidence bundle link
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Synthetic mixes may under- or over-estimate real customer tail behavior. Mitigation: Offer a trace-replay path where customers provide sanitized traces for a secondary verification run.

Risk: Autoscaler transient behavior during scale events can create noisy artifacts. Mitigation: Mark scale windows in manifest and run a separate steady-state segment ignoring scale transients for SLA checks.
Risk: GPU memory fragmentation causes inconsistent batch sizing. Mitigation: Add a memory-pressure probe and include memory allocations per-run; fail the run if fragmentation > threshold.
operational_steps: 1) Provision test fleet and billing project using onramp automation. 2) Upload or select traffic recipe (synthetic or trace). 3) Run calibration. 4) Execute signature runs (3x steady-state). 5) Execute stress scenarios (microbursts + scale triggers). 6) Collect artifacts and run acceptance checklist. 7) Submit evidence bundle to customer and schedule review. 8) If pass, create Dedicated capacity SLA attestation doc and enable onboarding label.
customer_communication_template: Hi <Customer>, we've completed the Dedicated throughput certification run. Attached is the evidence bundle (manifest, metrics CSV, dashboard snapshot). Key results: p95 latency X ms (target Y ms), tokens/sec Z, autoscaler events N. Please review the evidence and reply with acceptance or any questions. If accepted, we'll schedule go-live and update SLA paperwork.
